items.markdown:
Web content accessibility means `designing websites and digital tools so people with all types of disabilities can perceive, understand, navigate, and interact with them`.[[1]](https://www.w3.org/WAI/fundamentals/accessibility-intro/)

The worldwide standard for this is the [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/) , created by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_Content_Accessibility_Guidelines)[[2]](https://sdrc.rice.edu/web-accessibility-guidelines)

### Four Core Principles (POUR)

WCAG relies on four main rules, known by the acronym POUR:[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dRL_BOVuOzk&t=8)

- **Perceivable:** Information must be presented in ways users can sense (such as adding alt text for images or captions for videos).
- **Operable:** Interface parts and navigation must work for everyone (such as supporting full keyboard navigation).
- **Understandable:** Text and operation must be clear and predictable.
- **Robust:** Content must work well with current and future assistive tools, like screen readers.[[1]](https://www.ada.gov/resources/web-guidance/)[[2]](https://www.section508.gov/develop/guide-accessible-web-design-development/)[[3]](https://www.dpi.nc.gov/about-dpi/technology-services/digital-accessibility/wcag-21-level-aa)

### Three Levels of Conformance
Websites measure their adherence using three distinct tiers:[[1]](https://www.wcag.com/resource/what-is-wcag/)

- **Level A:** The minimum baseline requirement.
- **Level AA:** The widely accepted legal benchmark for laws like the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
- **Level AAA:** The highest and strictest tier, which is often difficult to apply to all types of content.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h5NFovz5Mpc&t=9)[[2]](https://www.wcag.com/resource/what-is-wcag/)[[3]](https://sdrc.rice.edu/web-accessibility-guidelines)

If you want to check your site, tell me:

- Do you want recommendations for **automated testing tools**?
- Are you looking to meet **Level A or Level AA** standards?
